reviews.text: I don’t leave reviews unless I’m truly upset I scheduled an appointment for my cat who was sick with some type of ear issue and I show up to my appointment just to be told by the lady at the front desk they don’t have record of me. Then it turned into they do have record of me under another number but I called to cancel my own appointment. I then explained to them I didn’t and wouldn’t cancel my appointment then it became well someone called and canceled your appointment. Long story short another lady comes in at my time spot and the lady at the desk rubs her dog and immediately puts her in a back room. So they canceled my appointment for my sick cat to get in I guess one of their regulars who had an issue and then lied to my face and said there was nothing they could do. I pleaded with them to at least just take a look at my cat because I understand what they had done and they said no. I left there wanting to cry. You do not treat people nor animals like that at all. I would never recommend this place. Stay away from people who do business this way.

Update: If you are looking for a new vet, please choose Heights Veterinary.  I urge you to not choose Thrive in the Heights.

Please read the last portion of my post especially as it is concerning. There are distinct Red Flags; please see below.

My experience with Thrive in the Heights started off okay about a year ago, but I quickly noticed lapses in communication and signs that this practice is poorly managed and poorly staffed.

Red Flag #1: No Returned Calls

One of my dogs requires daily medication to control her seizures. I began having problems trying to refill her medicine from the beginning with Thrive, and was consistently left stuck without it being approved by the vet in a timely manner, which ultimately meant that my dog will experience seizures. Frustrating, yes, but this kind of thing can be easily remedied with a prompt return phone call from their office along with an explanation of the delay and solution. They have failed to call me back more times than I can count, just for this one problem.

Red Flag #2: Vet Incompetence

After repeated refill problems, I went to their office to speak with Dr. Brian Smolik, because you guessed it-- No one would return my calls. When I communicated the delay in getting the refills, he admitted to me that he'd let his DEA license lapse and told me it was a hassle with the State, so he could not refill the medication. Another vet had to approve, which was fine, but I felt concerned. With the next sets of refills, the problem continued, and continued... No call-backs as I was promised, no long term remedy attempted at that time.

Red Flag #3: Inability to Solve Client Issues

By this point, I clearly and calmly told Thrive that I was not a happy customer due to the continuous hassle of trying to get simple refills of a very important medication. I asked to speak to the Practice Manager and the vet. I called at 8am and was told the Practice Manager was in surgery, and the vet was busy (I'll come back to the surgery part). I understood, and called back later in the afternoon twice to check back. Never got a return call.
I called back one last time that day around 5pm, and was put on hold for an entire eleven minutes-- Enough time for me to get in my car and drive to their office. Again, all I wanted was to speak with someone who would help me.
As I parked, I was still on hold...
Dr. Smolik met me at the door (still on hold at this point) and I again explained what was going on and that I didn't appreciate their lack of communication.

The Practice Manager came out to meet with me as the vet and I were talking. We went in a back office and she asked me to explain everything. I did, and she asked me what would solve the problem. I stated to her that all I need is to make sure my dog gets her medications refilled on time.

Red Flag #4: They Are *Very* Short-Staffed

The Practice Manager explained that the reason as to why I was experiencing poor communication is because "We are very short-staffed... We should be a team of twelve, but we are a team of five."

She continued to say, "I am not even a tech, and I am having to help with surgeries."
That is verbatim.

What? How exactly are you helping with surgeries? Are you performing tasks that a tech or a vet should be doing? Are you putting your clients' pets lives in danger?
By this time, I knew that I would not ever bring one of my dogs to them ever again.

I do not, will not, trust my pets' well-being with a practice that is understaffed and without proper veterinary professionals.  I will not do business with a practice that doesn't communicate and doesn't work to solve problems that are consistent ones.

Thanks for reading.
